summary.oneLiner: Dhampur Sugar Mills Limited is a long-established Uttar Pradesh-based integrated sugarcane processor engaged in manufacturing and dealing in sugar, power, industrial alcohol, ethanol, chemicals and potable spirit.
summary.business: The Company is engaged in dealing with and manufacturing of sugar, power, industrial alcohol, ethanol, chemicals and potable spirit, operating as an existing company incorporated on 22nd May, 1933. Its operations are cane-based and integrated: it generates renewable energy through its cogeneration facilities and has enhanced its ethanol production capacity to support the Government of India's Ethanol Blending Programme. It works closely with the farming community in its catchment areas, promoting sustainable agricultural practices and modern techniques to improve cane yield.

endMarkets: India - ethanol supplied under the Government of India's Ethanol Blending Programme|Uttar Pradesh cane catchment and surrounding rural communities where the manufacturing units operate

risks.risk: Policy dependence on the Government of India's Ethanol Blending Programme
risks.note: The Company has enhanced its ethanol production capacity specifically to support the Ethanol Blending Programme, so the returns on that capacity are tied to the continuation and terms of a government programme it does not control.

risks.risk: Changing labour legislation (the new Labour Codes)
risks.note: The Labour Codes affect the Company's operations and compliance requirements; management states it does not expect any material impact from their implementation, but the compliance burden and cost base remain exposed to how the Codes are enforced.

risks.risk: Water availability and the water intensity of sugarcane cultivation
risks.note: The Company encourages farmers to adopt modern agricultural techniques for reducing water consumption in sugarcane cultivation and supports rainwater harvesting and water conservation projects in its areas of operation, indicating that water is a structural constraint on its cane supply.

risks.risk: Environmental compliance - effluent discharge and air emissions at manufacturing units
risks.note: The Company has had to adopt measures towards achieving Zero Liquid Discharge, including installation of advanced treatment and recovery systems, to reduce and eliminate water and air pollution in the vicinity of its manufacturing units; continued compliance requires ongoing environmental investment.

risks.risk: Dependence on the farming community for cane supply and agronomic practice
risks.note: The Company actively promotes sustainable agricultural practices among farmers through awareness programmes and capacity-building initiatives, reflecting that raw-material availability and quality rest on third-party cultivators rather than on owned estates.

The Company depends on a skilled, motivated and engaged workforce across multiple locations and runs structured induction and continuous learning programmes; industrial relations remained cordial and harmonious during the year, but labour continuity is structural to a multi-unit seasonal operation.

The Company has adopted a Vigil Mechanism / Whistle Blower Policy to provide Directors and Employees a route to report unethical practices, fraud or violations of the Code of Conduct, with safeguards against victimisation - an explicit acknowledgement that conduct risk requires a standing control.

Mitigation rests on the Risk Management Policy and framework, whose effectiveness depends on identifying risks at an appropriate time; risk procedures are periodically reviewed and the risk-management strategy is integrated with overall business strategy and communicated throughout the organisation.

one-line thesis: Despite a 22% drop in cane crush and ethanol sales, Q4FY25 saw improved sugar realization and power margins, with potable spirits scaling up; the key shift is toward sugar over ethanol due to policy constraints and better pricing, with recovery expected only from FY27 via new cane varieties.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +0.41% YoY (INR2,655cr vs INR2,644cr); EBITDA: -36.1% YoY (INR187cr vs INR293cr); PAT (reported): -60.8% YoY (INR52.2cr vs INR132.9cr); PAT (normalized): exclude one-off power arrears (INR75cr PBT includes retroactive tariff benefit from Apr 2024); Order book: not disclosed; Net debt: not disclosed
guidance: Revenue growth: no explicit guidance; Margin: ethanol EBIT margin likely to remain low-single digits (3-5%) due to transfer pricing and maize mix; Order inflow: none disclosed; Capex/commissioning: no major capex planned for FY26-FY27
segment / subsidiary detail: Sugar: FY25 crush down 22% to 28.49L tons, production down 25% to 2.62L tons; Q4 crush up 6.2% to 16.76L tons; avg realization INR38,736/ton (+4% YoY); Ethanol: FY25 sales down 44% to 694L liters due to B-heavy/syrup restrictions; Q4 sales up 22% to 323L liters; Maize contribution 46% of total; Power: revenue up to 9.9% of total; EBIT contribution 49.3%; tariff revised +INR0.82/kWh effective Apr 2024 (retroactive benefit); Potable Spirits: production up 40% to 31.31L cases; Q4 production up 67% to 8.27L cases; Chemicals: marginal negative EBIT
growth verticals / optionality: Potable spirits capacity expansion (2 new tetra pack lines commissioned in FY25); potential ethanol volume recovery in FY26 with full maize utilization; long-term cane yield recovery from FY27 via varietal shift
margins & cost dynamics: Sugar margins improved due to higher realization (INR38.7k/ton) despite lower recovery (11.27% in Q4); Ethanol margins compressed to 3.8% (FY25) due to transfer pricing changes and lower B-heavy/syrup feedstock; Maize ethanol margins lower than sugar-based; Power margins boosted by retroactive tariff hike; Cane development costs rising slightly but not materially
capex / expansion: No major capex planned for FY26 or FY27; recent capex completed: 2 potable spirits lines (Apr & Dec 2024); focus is on cane development, not plant expansion
capital allocation: Board approved INR20cr buyback; no dividend guidance; focus on debt reduction and cane development budget; no M&A or new project funding announced
risks & watch-items: Cane yield volatility due to red rot and monsoon dependency; ethanol policy uncertainty (B-heavy/syrup pricing); maize input cost volatility; delayed recovery of pol in cane until FY27; regulatory delays in ethanol pricing (tenders only in Oct 2025)
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic on FY26 recovery; acknowledges structural challenges in cane yield; emphasizes long-term varietal shift (238 replacement); avoids giving hard guidance; highlights power tariff benefit as one-off; tone is defensive on ethanol margins and realistic on sugar recovery timeline
non-obvious takeaways: The retroactive power tariff hike (Apr 2024) boosted Q4 PBT by ~INR15-20cr, masking underlying operational weakness; maize ethanol is a capacity-utilization tool, not a margin driver; 238 replacement is a 4-5 year process, not a 1-year fix; farmers are not shifting away from sugarcane in Dhampur’s command area, contrary to industry rumors

moat.body:
- Long operating heritage - an existing company incorporated on 22nd May, 1933, holding its 91st Annual General Meeting
- Deep promoter and board continuity: Mr. Ashok Kumar Goel has served on the Board since 1969 with over 52 years of experience in the sugar and paper industries, and Mr. Gaurav Goel has been associated with the Board since 1994 with more than two decades in the sugar industry

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Demerger] "Demerger of Dhampur Sugar Mills Limited" is listed as a key milestone; the extract does not reliably bind it to a year and the deck gives no further detail on what was demerged.
- [Seasonality] The deck cautions that "Sugar being a seasonal industry, the quarter's performance may not be representative of the Company's annual performance."
- [Gross vs net revenue] The deck reports both Operating Revenue - Gross and Operating Revenue - Net (Rs 785.41 Cr and Rs 551.86 Cr standalone for Q1FY27), with potable spirits stated net of excise duty - the two are not interchangeable.
- [Regulatory/season] Power export fell on "early closure of SS 25-26", linking co-gen export volumes to the length of the crushing season.
